newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek brokers boycott bourse trade in protest.
newsitem.headline: Greek brokers boycott bourse trade in protest.

text.p: Angry Athens brokers voted at the bourse opening on Friday to boycott trading in a row with the bourse's clearing house, causing a total halt in trading.

The brokers were demanding that the clearing house guarantee settlement, after some brokers said the clearing house had failed to pay certain brokerages on Thursday. The clearing house has not commented on the brokers' allegations.
The general share index was stuck at 918.12, just off Thursday's 918.13 close, after just 5.6 million drachmas of trades on Friday before brokers voted to halt activity.

One broker said the boycott was aimed at putting pressure on the government to intervene and resolve the problem before it grew out of proportion. Brokers wanted to meet National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou.

"Instead of intervening fast to cover the cash problem which is of a relatively small magnitude and allow the system to keep on going, the government is being indecisive. This could grow into a big problem," said one broker who asked to remain anonymous.

Member firm Delta Securities was barred from trading on Thursday for non-compliance with settlement regulations. Someone who answered the Delta telephone on Thursday told Reuters there was no one around to comment and no one answered the Delta telephone on Friday.
